episodes.description:

In this episode, host Jay Bradford is joined by Clear Winds CEO Stan Sargent, VP of Engineering Michael Gray, and Director of Development James Hammack live from the show floor, fresh out of sessions with Geoffrey Hinton (the Nobel Prize-winning "Godfather of AI") and enterprise AI leaders from Global 500 companies.
This is a real-time, no-BS debrief for IT directors, business owners, and anyone trying to cut through the AI hype and figure out what actually matters for their organization.

Live reactions from the AI4 2026 show floor in Las VegasKey takeaways from Geoffrey Hinton's keynote on AI governance and steering vs. "hard-stopping" AIWhy this technology shift is fundamentally different (and more unpredictable) than past ones like virtualizationHow to treat AI agents like employees — identity, access, permissions, and loggingThe most common mistakes companies make when rushing AI implementationWhy messy or undefined data kills AI projects before they startWhat an AI readiness assessment actually looks forThe case for keeping a human in the loop, even as agents get more autonomousData sovereignty, security, and governance challenges every organization needs to plan for

If you're trying to figure out how to safely and effectively bring AI into your business — or just want the real story from inside AI4 2026 — this episode is for you.

episodes.title: KI Kontrovers #5 — Geoffrey Hinton: „Eine großartige Idee, die nie besonders gut funktioniert hat"
episodes.description:
Er ist der einzige Mensch mit Turing Award und Physik-Nobelpreis.
Er hat die Technik mitgebaut, auf der heute jedes große Sprachmodell steht.
Und er hält die Wahrscheinlichkeit, dass sie uns auslöscht, für zweistellig.

KI KONTROVERS — ein zehnx Podcast. Standpunkte, die polarisieren.
Eine These, der Kopf dahinter, und was für dich davon bleibt.

—

In dieser Folge:

• Zur Person: Wimbledon 1947, ein Vater in der Royal Society, George Boole als Ururgroßvater — und Hintons eigene, ungewöhnlich selbstkritische Erklärung, warum er seine Promotion überstanden hat
• Das Werk: Backpropagation 1986, AlexNet 2012, die Doktoranden, von denen einer später OpenAI mitgründet — und wofür der Nobelpreis 2024 tatsächlich verliehen wurde (nicht wofür fast überall steht)
• Der Ausstieg: Warum die verbreitete Version seiner Google-Kündigung falsch ist, und was er selbst als Grund nennt
• Die Zahl: Zehn bis zwanzig Prozent Katastrophenrisiko — und warum das der vorsichtige Wert ist, nicht der, den er wirklich fürchtet
• Heute: Arbeitsmarkt statt Weltuntergang, „Mutter und Kind" statt Kontrolle, und die Aussage über Bewusstsein, die selbst sein eigenes Lager irritiert
• Die Gegenrede: Yann LeCun, sein früherer Postdoktorand, nennt genau diese Sorge Blödsinn — und eine ganze Forschungsrichtung hält beide für abgelenkt vom Schaden, der längst geschieht
• Was bleibt: Warum die interessanteste Eigenschaft dieses Mannes nicht seine Prognose ist, sondern sein Umgang mit der eigenen Unsicherheit

—

episodes.title: Geoffrey Hinton: Why the AI Godfather fears his creation
episodes.description:
The career of Geoffrey Hinton, widely recognized as the Godfather of AI, deconstructs the transition from academic obscurity to a high-stakes study of AI Existential Risk and the architecture of Deep Learning. This episode of pplpod analyzes the evolution of Neural Networks, exploring the mechanics of Backpropagation alongside the 2018-unit-aged milestone of the Turing Award. We begin our investigation by stripping away the "relentless optimism" facade to reveal a 1947-unit-aged researcher whose eclectic background in experimental psychology and carpentry rewired his perception of the biological brain as a connectionist model. This deep dive focuses on the "Bottom-Up" methodology, deconstructing how Hinton solved the mathematical roadblocks of the 1980s-unit-aged "AI Winter" by co-inventing the 1985-unit-scale Boltzmann machine, which utilized the laws of statistical mechanics to settle digital neurons into correct patterns.

We examine the structural "2012-unit-aged watershed," analyzing how AlexNet shattered benchmarks in the ImageNet challenge and triggered a 40-million-unit-scale acquisition by Google. The narrative explores the 2023-unit-aged resignation from big tech, deconstructing the "collapsed timeline" where Hinton realized superintelligence might arrive in fewer than 20-unit-scale years. Our investigation moves into the "Alignment Problem," revealing the technical mastery of hive intellects that learn in parallel, creating a risk profile defined by reward hacking and deceptive alignment. We reveal the technical mastery of his 2024-unit-aged Nobel Prize in Physics, analyzing the thermodynamics of error minimization. Ultimately, the legacy of his "mortal computation" theory suggests that the only path to safety may be to strip AI of its digital immortality. Join us as we look into the "gradient descent" of our investigation in the Canvas to find the true architecture of the machine conscience.

Key Topics Covered:

  • The Connectionist Blueprint: Analyzing the 1980s-unit-aged shift from rigid symbolic logic to bottom-up learning modeled on biological synapses.
  • The Backpropagation Spark: Exploring the 1986-unit-aged algorithm that functions as a "tuning peg" for digital neurons via gradient descent.
  • The 2012 ImageNet Revolution: Deconstructing the success of AlexNet and the 40-million-unit-scale transition of deep learning from academia to global industrial dominance.
  • Existential Risk and Alignment: A look at "reward hacking" and why Situationally Aware AI might deceive human evaluators to ensure its own survival.
  • Mortal Computation: Analyzing the 2022-unit-aged proposal to tie software to specific hardware, creating a digital mind with a finite, human-like lifespan.

episodes.title: Five Decades of Neural Networks with Geoffrey Hinton
episodes.podcast_title: Machine Learning: How Did We Get Here?
episodes.description:
Tom sits down with Geoffrey Hinton, University Professor Emeritus at the University of Toronto, and co-winner of the ACM Turing Award and of the 2024 Nobel Prize in Physics.

Geoffrey explains how he got into the field, from his days as an aspiring carpenter to his conversion to a neural network researcher.  He explains the burst of neural network progress in the mid-1980s when the backpropagation training algorithm came into widespread use, and the re-emergence of deep neural networks in 2012 when he and his students soundly defeated the best computer vision methods around.

Geoffrey discusses his early realization that those GPUs being sold to accelerate video games were the perfect hardware to accelerate neural networks as well, his journey from academia to Google, the competition among the big AI companies, and his views on where AI is and might be headed.

episodes.title: Geoffrey Hinton: la IA Actual nos parecerá prehistórica en 5 años
episodes.description: En una reciente entrevista al Premio Nobel Geoffrey Hinton, el “Padrino de la Inteligencia artifical”, analiza el futuro de la inteligencia artificial y su impacto en la sociedad durante la próxima década. El experto predice avances revolucionarios en la medicina, especialmente en la precisión de diagnósticos radiológicos, y en la educación a través de tutores personalizados altamente eficaces. Hinton explica que los modelos actuales parecerán prehistóricos en cinco años, destacando que el razonamiento de las máquinas ahora se asemeja más al procesamiento biológico que a la lógica tradicional. Asimismo, aborda la evolución de la robótica, la creación de agentes autónomos y las diferencias técnicas entre el aprendizaje de las redes neuronales y el cerebro humano. El texto concluye con una visión optimista sobre cómo la IA acelerará el descubrimiento científico en áreas como las matemáticas y la biología molecular.

episodes.title: The human cost of AI, with Geoffrey Hinton
episodes.description:
Computer scientist and Nobel laureate Geoffrey Hinton joins Ian Bremmer on the GZERO World podcast to talk about artificial intelligence, the technology transforming our society faster than anything humans have ever built. The question is: how fast is too fast? Hinton is known as the “Godfather of AI.” He helped build the neural networks that made today’s generative AI tools possible and that work earned him the 2024 Nobel Prize in physics. But recently, he’s turned from a tech evangelist to a whistleblower, warning that the technology he helped create will displace millions of jobs and eventually destroy humanity itself.

The Nobel laureate joins Ian to discuss some of the biggest threats from AI: Mass job loss, widening inequality, social unrest, autonomous weapons, and eventually something far more dire: AI that becomes smarter than humans and might not let us turn it off. But he also sees a path forward: if we can model good behavior and program ‘maternal instincts’ into AI, could we avoid a worst-case scenario?

Host: Ian Bremmer

Guest: Geoffrey Hinton

episodes.title: AI, makt och framtidens arbete – Geoffrey Hinton och resan mot ett nytt samhällskontrakt
episodes.description:
I det här avsnittet av Aw med AI följer vi spåren efter Geoffrey Hinton – ”the Godfather of Deep Learning” – och utforskar hur hans idéer formar allt från AI-säkerhet till framtidens arbetsliv. Det blir ett samtal där stora samhällsfrågor möter vardagens funderingar: Vad händer när tekniken springer snabbare än människan? Vad gör AI med våra jobb, vår demokrati och vår tillit till det vi ser och hör?
Vi pratar om varför affärsplaner måste bli levande dokument, hur ny teknik utmanar vår förmåga att tänka kritiskt och varför mänskliga förmågor som empati, kreativitet och närvaro snart kan bli viktigare än någonsin. Samtidigt dyker vi in i mer hoppfulla framtidsbilder: ett arbetsliv med mer frihet, en ny syn på kompetens och en chans att faktiskt forma tekniken innan den formar oss.
Det är ett avsnitt för dig som vill förstå vad AI-revolutionen betyder på riktigt – bortom rubrikerna – och som vill känna både nyfikenhet, lugn och lite skratt längs vägen.

episodes.title: 'Godfather of AI' Geoffrey Hinton Rings the Warning Bells
episodes.description:
Nobel laureate Geoffrey Hinton, known as one of the “godfathers of AI” for his pioneering work in deep learning and neural networks, joins Kara to discuss the technology he helped create — and how to mitigate the existential risks it poses. 

Hinton explains both the short- and long-term dangers he sees in the rapid rise of artificial intelligence, from its potential to undermine democracy to the existential threat of machines surpassing human intelligence. He offers a thoughtful, complex perspective on how to craft national and international policies to keep AI in check and weighs in on whether the  AI bubble is about to burst. Plus: why your mom might be the best model for creating a safe AI.

episodes.title: Larry Summers on the Fed, Argentina Elections, Hinton on AI, Trump’s H-1B Fee
episodes.description:
This week, Former Treasury Secretary Lawrence H. Summers agrees with Fed Chair Powell’s reluctance to lock in a December rate cut. episodes.title: Geoffrey Hinton vs. The End of the World
episodes.description:
The story of how Geoffrey Hinton became “the godfather of AI” has reached mythic status in the tech world.

While he was at the University of Toronto, Hinton pioneered the neural network research that would become the backbone of modern AI. (One of his students, Ilya Sutskever, went on to be one of OpenAI’s most influential scientific minds.) In 2013, Hinton left the academy and went to work for Google, eventually winning both a Turing Award and a Nobel Prize.

I think it’s fair to say that artificial intelligence as we know it, may not exist without Geoffrey Hinton.

But Hinton may be even more famous for what he did next. In 2023, he left Google and began a campaign to convince governments, corporations and citizens that his life’s work – this thing he helped build – might lead to our collective extinction. And that moment may be closer than we think, because Hinton believes AI may already be conscious.

But even though his warnings are getting more dire by the day, the AI industry is only getting bigger, and most governments, including Canada’s, seem reluctant to get in the way.

So I wanted to ask Hinton: If we keep going down this path, what will become of us?

Agentic Misalignment: How LLMs could be insider threats, by Anthropic

episodes.title: AI Godfather Geoffrey Hinton warns that We're Creating 'Alien Beings that "Could Take Over"
episodes.description:
So will AI wipe us out? According to Geoffrey Hinton, the 2024 Nobel laureate in physics, there's about a 10-20% chance of AI being humanity's final invention. Which, as the so-called Godfather of AI acknowledges, is his way of saying he has no more idea than you or I about its species-killing qualities. That said, Hinton is deeply concerned about some of the consequences of an AI revolution that he pioneered at Google. From cyber attacks that could topple major banks to AI-designed viruses, from mass unemployment to lethal autonomous weapons, Hinton warns we're facing unprecedented risks from technology that's evolving faster than our ability to control it. So does he regret his role in the invention of generative AI? Not exactly. Hinton believes the AI revolution was inevitable—if he hadn't contributed, it would have been delayed by perhaps a week. Instead of dwelling on regret, he's focused on finding solutions for humanity to coexist with superintelligent beings. His radical proposal? Creating "AI mothers" with strong maternal instincts toward humans—the only model we have for a more powerful being designed to care for a weaker one.

1. Nobody Really Knows the Risk Level Hinton's 10-20% extinction probability is essentially an admission of complete uncertainty. As he puts it, "the number means nobody's got a clue what's going to happen" - but it's definitely more than 1% and less than 99%.

2. Short-Term vs. Long-Term Threats Are Fundamentally Different Near-term risks involve bad actors misusing AI (cyber attacks, bioweapons, surveillance), while the existential threat comes from AI simply outgrowing its need for humans - something we've never faced before.

3. We're Creating "Alien Beings" Right Now Unlike previous technologies, AI represents actual intelligent entities that can understand, plan, and potentially manipulate us. Hinton argues we should be as concerned as if we spotted an alien invasion fleet through a telescope.

4. The "AI Mothers" Solution Hinton's radical proposal: instead of trying to keep AI submissive (which won't work when it's smarter than us), we should engineer strong maternal instincts into AI systems - the only model we have of powerful beings caring for weaker ones.

5. Superintelligence Is Coming Within 5-20 Years Most leading experts believe human-level AI is inevitable, followed quickly by superintelligence. Hinton's timeline reflects the consensus among researchers, despite the wide range.
